entries.title: Stepper and rail encode done differently
entries.reason: The encodings really differ: 'done' is an outlined circle with a green tick in the stepper (Stepper.tsx:55,64) but a filled green circle in the rail (VerificationRail.tsx:52,79), and 'current' is a ring with a number versus a dot, even though the rail's own comment claims 'the same circles'. The rail is only visible at 2xl or wider, and the 1.4 shell (status chips plus bottom tool bar, with the chip component from 1.5) replaces both components, so it should not be built twice; the badge wording already has one source in workflow-steps.ts.

entries.title: Badge detail hidden only in the hover title
New one-off values for type and shape without a system
entries.reason: Does not apply: the values named are the decided scale, not drift. DESIGN.md §1.2 sets for the workspace 22px/800/-0.02em (project title), 15px/700 (section title h2), 14px/700, 13px/500 and 11px/600 - text-[22px] (components/workspace/WorkspaceShell.tsx:110, WorkspaceListReport.tsx:378, app/(app)/admin/design-system/page.tsx:173) and text-[15px] (WorkspaceListReport.tsx:238, design-system/page.tsx:163) implement exactly that. DESIGN.md §1.5 says 'height 32px compact, 40px cozy' - that is min-h-[32px]/min-h-[40px] in components/cc/Button.tsx:45-46 and Field.tsx:63. text-[0.85em] (components/PresentationViewer.tsx:49) is inline code that deliberately scales with the parent type. The report refutes itself here: its coverage_notes call the same tokens 'bewusstes neues Vokabular fuer 1.5, kein Drift'. The only real remainder: text-[16px] in components/cc/MessageBox.tsx:126 is not in the scale of §1.2 - that belongs in the style guard of 1.5, not in a finding of its own.

entries.title: New one-off tokens without a connection to the system
entries.reason: Duplicate of [774b8eb5bbac] / UX-111 and refuted for the same reason: the same token list from the design scan, only reported as 'consistency' instead of 'typography'. The values are in DESIGN.md §1.2 (22/15/14/13/11 px) and §1.5 (32/40 px button height) and live in the admin-gated cc library (components/cc/*, components/workspace/*, app/(app)/admin/design-system/page.tsx); shadow-[inset_3px_0_0_var(--cc-code-hl-bar)] in components/cc/CodeSurface.tsx:68 uses the variable declared in app/globals.css:195 and is DESIGN.md §1.1 'left 3px #93c5fd, marked line'.

entries.title: New arbitrary font sizes without binding to the scale
entries.reason: Duplicate of [774b8eb5bbac] / UX-111 and [76fa16657ade] / UX-112 - the same four type sizes a third time. Refuted as there: text-[22px] and text-[15px] are the workspace scale decided in DESIGN.md §1.2, text-[0.85em] is deliberately em-relative inline code (components/PresentationViewer.tsx:49). The finding already concedes violet-400 as deliberate and could have drawn the same conclusion for the remaining values; the coverage_notes of the same report do.

entries.title: Existing dark setting without a way back after the switch was removed
entries.reason: Refuted: a stored dark value is inert. No code in app/, components/, hooks/ or lib/ adds or toggles the 'dark' class or reads profile.theme (grep over all .ts/.tsx finds none), and tests/dark-mode-guard.spec.ts holds that line from four sides: no dark: variant anywhere (:77), no .dark rule in any stylesheet (:89), nothing wires a theme up again (:97), and on the rendered page 'forcing class="dark" onto the document changes no colour' (:137). A user with theme=dark on their profile sees exactly the light product; there is nothing to be trapped in.

entries.reason: Premise does not hold: the choice is remembered. Not now writes cc.terms.declined.<version> to sessionStorage (components/TermsReacceptGate.tsx:69,87) and the card does not come back on the next route; accept is recorded server-side and ends it for good. The screenshots show the card on every route because the capture never clicks either button. The banner-with-dialog recommendation contradicts the component's stated rule (lines 32-45): while declining is a real option the dialogue asks and takes Not now; once the accepted version is ended it blocks, because a dismissible notice would leave somebody in a product that answers 403 everywhere.

entries.title: ToS box pushes work content below the fold
entries.reason: Recommends what already exists: the Not now state is remembered per browsing session (components/TermsReacceptGate.tsx:69,87, key cc.terms.declined.<version>); the first viewport is filled once per session until a choice is made, not on every route. Same evidence and same capture artefact as 11568f20ad9d.

entries.title: ToS notice pushes out the work area in the first viewport
entries.reason: The one part not already true: cross-session memory of Not now. Session scope is the documented promise (components/TermsReacceptGate.tsx:60-64) and re-asking each new session while an amendment is pending is deliberate; remembering it across sessions means an account-level decline record and is Sonny's call, not a UX fix. Everything else in the finding is answered by 11568f20ad9d.
